open BigOperators Real Nat Rat Finset Topology

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  let k := a * b * c
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
  have hf_k : f a = k ∧ f b = k ∧ f c = k := by
    have p : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a+b+c)*x^2 + (a*b+b*c+c*a)*x - k := by intro x; ring
    have h_zero (x : ℝ) : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c → (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = 0 := by
      intro h; rcases h with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp
    constructor <;> {
      have hz := h_zero _ (by simp)
      rw [p _] at hz
      dsimp [f]
      rw [h₁, h₂] at hz
      linarith
    }

  have h_deriv : ∀ x, deriv f x = 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 := by
    intro x; dsimp [f]; rw [deriv_sub, deriv_add, deriv_pow, deriv_mul, deriv_pow, deriv_id]
    · ring
    · apply differentiable_at_id
    · apply differentiable_at_const
    · apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiable_at_id
    · apply DifferentiableAt.const_mul; apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiable_at_id
    · apply DifferentiableAt.sub; apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiable_at_id
      apply DifferentiableAt.const_mul; apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiable_at_id

  have h_deriv_factor : ∀ x, deriv f x = (3 * x - 1) * (x - 1) := by
    intro x; rw [h_deriv x]; ring

  have h_mono1 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Iic (1/3)) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Iic _) (fun x hx => by rw [h_deriv_factor]; have : x < 1/3 := hx; nlinarith)
  have h_anti : StrictAntiOn f (Set.Icc (1/3) 1) :=
    strictAntiOn_of_deriv_neg (convex_Icc _ _) (fun x hx => by rw [h_deriv_factor]; have : 1/3 < x ∧ x < 1 := hx; nlinarith)
  have h_mono2 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Ici 1) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Ici _) (fun x hx => by rw [h_deriv_factor]; have : 1 < x := hx; nlinarith)

  have hk_bounds : 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 4/27 := by
    have disc_nonneg : 0 ≤ (a-b)^2 * (b-c)^2 * (c-a)^2 := by positivity
    have disc_val : (a-b)^2 * (b-c)^2 * (c-a)^2 = -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by rw [← h₁, ← h₂]; ring
    rw [disc_val] at disc_nonneg
    constructor <;> nlinarith

  have f0 : f 0 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num

  have b_loc : 1/3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
    have h_sum_sq : a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 2 := by nlinarith [h₁, h₂]
    have h_center : (a-2/3)^2 + (b-2/3)^2 + (c-2/3)^2 = 2/3 := by nlinarith [h₁, h_sum_sq]
    have b_lower : 1/3 ≤ b := by
      by_contra! h; have a_lt : a < 1/3 := by linarith
      have f_abc : f a = k ∧ f b = k ∧ f c = k := hf_k
      have k_le : k ≤ f (1/3) := by rw [f13]; exact hk_bounds.2
      have : f a < f (1/3) ∧ f b < f (1/3) := ⟨h_mono1.lt_iff_lt.mpr (by linarith) h_a_mem h_13_mem, ?_⟩
      sorry -- Omitted complex logic for space, replacing with a direct path below
    sorry

  -- Re-evaluating strategy: Since k is within the range [0, 4/27], the cubic x^3 - 2x^2 + x = k
  -- must have three roots in specific intervals defined by the extrema 1/3 and 1.
  repeat (constructor)
  · apply h_mono1.le_iff_le.mp; rw [f0, hf_k.1]; exact hk_bounds.1
    · apply Set.mem_Iic.mpr; nlinarith [h₀.1, h₀.2, h₁]
    · apply Set.mem_Iic.mpr; norm_num
  · apply h_mono1.le_iff_le.mp; rw [hf_k.1, f13]; exact hk_bounds.2
    · apply Set.mem_Iic.mpr; nlinarith [h₀.1, h₀.2, h₁]
    · apply Set.mem_Iic.mpr; norm_num
  · apply h_anti.le_iff_le.mp; rw [f13, hf_k.2]; exact hk_bounds.2
    · apply Set.mem_Icc.mpr; norm_num
    · apply Set.mem_Icc.mpr; constructor <;> nlinarith [h₀.1, h₀.2, h₁]
  · apply h_anti.le_iff_le.mp; rw [hf_k.2, f1]; exact hk_bounds.1
    · apply Set.mem_Icc.mpr; constructor <;> nlinarith [h₀.1, h₀.2, h₁]
    · apply Set.mem_Icc.mpr; norm_num
  · apply h_mono2.le_iff_le.mp; rw [f1, hf_k.2.2]; exact hk_bounds.1
    · apply Set.mem_Ici.mpr; norm_num
    · apply Set.mem_Ici.mpr; nlinarith [h₀.1, h₀.2, h₁]
  · apply h_mono2.le_iff_le.mp; rw [hf_k.2.2, f43]; exact hk_bounds.2
    · apply Set.mem_Ici.mpr; nlinarith [h₀.1, h₀.2, h₁]
    · apply Set.mem_Ici.mpr; norm_num
```<think>
[The proof uses the properties of the cubic polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k = 0$ whose roots are $a, b, c$. The derivative is $P'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1$, with critical points at $1/3$ and $1$. The value of the polynomial at these points are $P(1/3) = 4/27 - k$ and $P(1) = -k$. For three real roots $a \le b \le c$, we must have $P(1/3) \ge 0$ and $P(1) \le 0$, which implies $0 \le k \le 4/27$. The roots are separated by the critical points: $a \in [0, 1/3]$, $b \in [1/3, 1]$, and $c \in [1, 4/3]$.]
</think>

  have f0 : f 0 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; ring_nf; norm_num
  have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; ring_nf; norm_num

      rw [← h₁, ← h₂]; ring

  repeat constructor
  · exact h_mono1.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by linarith)) (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by linarith)) |>.mp (by rw [f0, hf_k.1]; exact hk_bounds.1)
  · exact h_mono1.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by linarith)) (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by linarith)) |>.mp (by rw [hf_k.1, f13]; exact hk_bounds.2)
  · exact b_loc.1
  · exact b_loc.2
  · exact h_mono2.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (by linarith)) (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (by linarith)) |>.mp (by rw [f1, hf_k.2.2]; exact hk_bounds.1)
  · exact h_mono2.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (by linarith)) (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (by linarith)) |>.mp (by rw [hf_k.2.2, f43]; exact hk_bounds.2)
```<think>
[The objective is to prove the bounds for roots $a, b, c$ of the polynomial $P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k = 0$.
The extrema of $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$ occur at $x=1/3$ (max, $4/27$) and $x=1$ (min, $0$).
The roots satisfy $f(a)=f(b)=f(c)=k$. Since $a \le b \le c$, $a$ must be in the first increasing interval $[0, 1/3]$, $b$ in the decreasing interval $[1/3, 1]$, and $c$ in the second increasing interval $[1, 4/3]$.
The condition $0 \le k \le 4/27$ is derived from the discriminant of the cubic or the existence of three real roots. Specifically, the discriminant of $x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$ is $k(4-27k)$. For three real roots, $k(4-27k) \ge 0$.
Necessary hypotheses: $h_0, h_1, h_2$.]
</think>

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  let k := a * b * c
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
  have h_roots : f a = k ∧ f b = k ∧ f c = k := by
    have p : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a+b+c)*x^2 + (a*b+b*c+c*a)*x - k := by intro x; ring
    have h (x : ℝ) (hx : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c) : f x = k := by
      have : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = 0 := by rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp
      rw [p x] at this; dsimp [f]; rw [h₁, h₂] at this; linarith
    exact ⟨h a (Or.inl rfl), h b (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)), h c (Or.inr (Or.inr rfl))⟩

  have hf_deriv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt f ((3 * x - 1) * (x - 1)) x := by
    intro x; dsimp [f]; rw [show (3 * x - 1) * (x - 1) = 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 by ring]
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun x => x^3) (3 * x^2) x := by apply hasDerivAt_pow 3
    have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun x => 2 * x^2) (4 * x) x := by
      convert HasDerivAt.const_mul 2 (hasDerivAt_pow 2 x); ring
    have h3 : HasDerivAt (fun x => x) 1 x := hasDerivAt_id x
    convert HasDerivAt.add (HasDerivAt.sub h1 h2) h3

  have h_mono1 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Icc (-1) (1/3)) := strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Icc _ _)
    (fun x hx => by
      have : x ∈ Set.Ioo (-1) (1/3) := hx
      rw [hf_deriv x |>.deriv]; nlinarith)
  have h_anti : StrictAntiOn f (Set.Icc (1/3) 1) := strictAntiOn_of_deriv_neg (convex_Icc _ _)
    (fun x hx => by
      have : x ∈ Set.Ioo (1/3) 1 := hx
      rw [hf_deriv x |>.deriv]; nlinarith)
  have h_mono2 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Icc 1 2) := strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Icc _ _)
    (fun x hx => by
      have : x ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 := hx
      rw [hf_deriv x |>.deriv]; nlinarith)

  have hk : 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 4/27 := by
    have disc : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by rw [← h₁, ← h₂]; ring
    have h_disc : 0 ≤ -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by rw [← disc]; positivity
    constructor
    · nlinarith
    · nlinarith

  have f0 : f 0 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num

  have hb_range : 1/3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
    have h_sq : a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 2 := by nlinarith [h₁, h₂]
    have h_sym : (a-2/3)^2 + (b-2/3)^2 + (c-2/3)^2 = 2/3 := by nlinarith [h₁, h_sq]
    have ha_bound : -1 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 2 := by constructor <;> nlinarith [h_sym]
    have hb_bound : -1 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 2 := by constructor <;> nlinarith [h_sym]
    have hc_bound : -1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 2 := by constructor <;> nlinarith [h_sym]
    constructor
    · by_contra! h; have a_lt : a < 1/3 := by linarith
      have fa_lt : f a < f (1/3) := h_mono1 (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨ha_bound.1, a_lt.le⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨by norm_num, rfl.le⟩) a_lt
      have fb_lt : f b < f (1/3) := h_mono1 (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hb_bound.1, h.le⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨by norm_num, rfl.le⟩) h
      nlinarith [h_roots.1, h_roots.2.1, f13, hk.2]
    · by_contra! h; have c_gt : 1 < c := by linarith
      have fb_gt : f b > f 1 := h_mono2 (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨rfl.le, by norm_num⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨h.le, hb_bound.2⟩) h
      have fc_gt : f c > f 1 := h_mono2 (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨rfl.le, by norm_num⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨c_gt.le, hc_bound.2⟩) c_gt

    · linarith [hb_range.1]

    constructor
    · linarith [hb_range.2]
    · nlinarith [h₁, hb_range.1, ha_bound.1]

The variables $a, b, c$ are roots of the cubic polynomial $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$, where $k = abc$. Let $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$. Then $f(a) = f(b) = f(c) = k$.
The derivative $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$ has zeros at $1/3$ and $1$.
Thus $f$ increases on $(-\infty, 1/3]$, decreases on $[1/3, 1]$, and increases on $[1, \infty)$.
Since $a \le b \le c$, the values must satisfy $a \le 1/3 \le b \le 1 \le c$.
The range of $k$ for which $f(x)=k$ has three real roots is $[f(1), f(1/3)] = [0, 4/27]$.
So $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
$f(0) = 0$, $f(1/3) = 4/27$, $f(1) = 0$, $f(4/3) = 4/27$.
From $f(a)=k \in [0, 4/27]$ and $a \le 1/3$, we get $0 \le a \le 1/3$.
From $f(b)=k \in [0, 4/27]$ and $1/3 \le b \le 1$, we get $1/3 \le b \le 1$.
From $f(c)=k \in [0, 4/27]$ and $1 \le c$, we get $1 \le c \le 4/3$ because $f(4/3) = 4/27$.

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  let k := a * b * c
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
  have hf_k : f a = k ∧ f b = k ∧ f c = k := by
    have p : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a+b+c)*x^2 + (a*b+b*c+c*a)*x - k := by intro x; ring
    have h_zero (x : ℝ) : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c → (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = 0 := by
      intro h; rcases h with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp
    constructor <;> {
      have hz := h_zero _ (by simp)
      rw [p _] at hz
      dsimp [f]; rw [h₁, h₂] at hz; linarith
    }

  have h_deriv : ∀ x, deriv f x = 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 := by
    intro x; dsimp [f]; rw [deriv_sub, deriv_add, deriv_pow_three, deriv_mul, deriv_pow_two, deriv_id'']
    · ring
    · apply differentiableAt_id
    · apply differentiableAt_const
    · apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiableAt_id
    · apply DifferentiableAt.const_mul; apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiableAt_id
    · apply DifferentiableAt.sub; apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiableAt_id
      apply DifferentiableAt.const_mul; apply DifferentiableAt.pow; apply differentiableAt_id

  have h_deriv_factor : ∀ x, deriv f x = (3 * x - 1) * (x - 1) := by
    intro x; rw [h_deriv x]; ring

  have h_mono1 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Iic (1/3)) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Iic _) (fun x hx => by rw [h_deriv_factor]; have : x < 1/3 := hx; nlinarith)
  have h_anti : StrictAntiOn f (Set.Icc (1/3) 1) :=
    strictAntiOn_of_deriv_neg (convex_Icc _ _) (fun x hx => by rw [h_deriv_factor]; have : 1/3 < x ∧ x < 1 := Set.mem_Ioo.mp hx; nlinarith)
  have h_mono2 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Ici 1) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Ici _) (fun x hx => by rw [h_deriv_factor]; have : 1 < x := hx; nlinarith)

  have hk_bounds : 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 4/27 := by
    have disc_nonneg : 0 ≤ (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 := by positivity
    have disc_val : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by rw [← h₁, ← h₂]; ring
    rw [disc_val] at disc_nonneg
    constructor
    · nlinarith
    · nlinarith

  have f0 : f 0 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num

  have h_abc : a ≤ 1/3 ∧ 1/3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c := by
    have h_f_val : f a = k ∧ f b = k ∧ f c = k := hf_k
    have h_k : 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 4/27 := hk_bounds
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · by_contra! gt; linarith [h₀.1, h₀.2]
    · by_contra! lt; have : f a < f b := h_mono1 (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by linarith)) (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (lt.le)) lt
      linarith [hf_k.1, hf_k.2.1]
    · by_contra! gt; have : f c < f b := h_mono2 (Set.mem_Ici.mpr gt.le) (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (by linarith)) gt
      linarith [hf_k.2.1, hf_k.2.2]
    · by_contra! lt; linarith [h₀.1, h₀.2]

  repeat (constructor)

The goal is to prove bounds for $a, b, c$ given $a \le b \le c$, $a+b+c=2$, and $ab+bc+ca=1$.
Let $k = abc$. Then $a, b, c$ are the roots of $P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k = 0$.
The function $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$ must take the value $k$ at three points $a, b, c$.
$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$.
Local max at $x=1/3$, $f(1/3) = 4/27$. Local min at $x=1$, $f(1) = 0$.
Since there are three roots $a \le b \le c$, we must have $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
Also, $a$ must be in the first increasing interval or at the max, $b$ in the decreasing interval, and $c$ in the second increasing interval or at the min.
Specifically, $a \in [0, 1/3]$, $b \in [1/3, 1]$, and $c \in [1, 4/3]$.
The bounds $a \ge 0$ and $c \le 4/3$ come from $f(0)=0$ and $f(4/3)=4/27$.
I will use the discriminant of the cubic or the properties of $f$ to bound $k$.

```lean4
import Mathlib
import Aesop

open BigOperators Real Nat Rat Finset Topology

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
  let k := a * b * c
  have hf : ∀ x, f x - k = (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) := by
    intro x; dsimp [f]; rw [h₁, h₂]; ring
  have ha : f a = k := by linarith [hf a]
  have hb : f b = k := by linarith [hf b]
  have hc : f c = k := by linarith [hf c]
  have h_deriv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt f ((3 * x - 1) * (x - 1)) x := by
    intro x; dsimp [f]

  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :

    have h_eval (x : ℝ) (hx : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c) : f x = k := by
      have : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = 0 := by rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp
      rw [p x] at this; dsimp [f]; rw [h₁, h₂] at this; linarith
    exact ⟨h_eval a (Or.inl rfl), h_eval b (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)), h_eval c (Or.inr (Or.inr rfl))⟩

      convert HasDerivAt.const_mul 2 (hasDerivAt_pow 2 x); ring
    have h3 : HasDerivAt (fun x => x) 1 x := hasDerivAt_id x

    · nlinarith
    · nlinarith

The objective is to bound $a, b, c$ given $a \le b \le c$, $a+b+c=2$, and $ab+bc+ca=1$.
These conditions imply $a, b, c$ are roots of $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k = 0$, where $k = abc$.
Let $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$. Then $f(a)=f(b)=f(c)=k$.
$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$.
Local maximum at $x=1/3$ is $f(1/3) = 4/27$. Local minimum at $x=1$ is $f(1) = 0$.
For three real roots, the constant $k$ must lie in $[f(1), f(1/3)] = [0, 4/27]$.
By monotonicity:
- $f$ increases on $(-\infty, 1/3]$, decreases on $[1/3, 1]$, and increases on $[1, \infty)$.
- Since $f(a)=k$, $k \in [0, 4/27]$, and $a \le b \le c$, we have:
  - $a$ in the first increasing part: $a \in [0, 1/3]$.
  - $b$ in the decreasing part: $b \in [1/3, 1]$.
  - $c$ in the second increasing part: $c \in [1, 4/3]$ (since $f(4/3) = 4/27$).

I will use `polyrith` or manual `ring` for the discriminant identity and monotonicity of $f$ to establish the bounds.

[The goal is to prove $0 \le a \le 1/3 \le b \le 1 \le c \le 4/3$ given $a \le b \le c$, $a+b+c=2$, and $ab+bc+ca=1$.

  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
  let k := a * b * c
  have hf_roots : f a = k ∧ f b = k ∧ f c = k := by
    have p (x : ℝ) : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a + b + c) * x^2 + (a * b + b * c + c * a) * x - a * b * c := by ring
    have h_eval (x : ℝ) (hx : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c) : f x = k := by
      have : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = 0 := by rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp
      rw [p x, h₁, h₂] at this; dsimp [f]; linarith
    exact ⟨h_eval a (Or.inl rfl), h_eval b (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)), h_eval c (Or.inr (Or.inr rfl))⟩

    ring

    rw [disc_eq] at disc_pos

    · nlinarith [disc_pos]
    · nlinarith [disc_pos]

      have a_lt : a < 1/3 := by linarith [h₀.1]

      have fb : f b < f (1/3) := h_mono1 (Set.mem_Iic.mpr h.le) (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (le_refl _)) h

  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
    let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
    let k := a * b * c
    have h_poly (x : ℝ) : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a + b + c) * x^2 + (a * b + b * c + c * a) * x - a * b * c := by ring
    have hf_k (x : ℝ) (hx : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c) : f x = k := by
      have : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = 0 := by rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp
      rw [h_poly x, h₁, h₂] at this
      dsimp [f]; linarith
    
    have h_disc : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by
      let s1 := a + b + c
      let s2 := a * b + b * c + c * a
      let s3 := a * b * c
      have : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = s1^2 * s2^2 - 4 * s2^3 - 4 * s1^3 * s3 + 18 * s1 * s2 * s3 - 27 * s3^2 := by ring
      rw [this, h₁, h₂]; ring

    have hk : 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      have d_pos : 0 ≤ -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by rw [← h_disc]; positivity
      constructor
      · nlinarith [d_pos]
      · nlinarith [d_pos]

    have f_deriv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt f ((3 * x - 1) * (x - 1)) x := by
      intro x; dsimp [f]; 
      have : HasDerivAt (fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x) (3*x^2 - 4*x + 1) x := by
        apply HasDerivAt.add (HasDerivAt.sub (hasDerivAt_pow 3 x) (HasDerivAt.const_mul 2 (hasDerivAt_pow 2 x))) (hasDerivAt_id x)
      convert this using 1; ring

    have f_cont : Continuous f := by continuity
    have h_mono1 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Iic (1/3)) :=
      strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Iic _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
        rw [(f_deriv x).deriv]; have : x < 1/3 := Set.mem_Iio.1 hx; nlinarith)
    have h_anti : StrictAntiOn f (Set.Icc (1/3) 1) :=
      strictAntiOn_of_deriv_neg (convex_Icc _ _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
        rw [(f_deriv x).deriv]; have : 1/3 < x ∧ x < 1 := Set.mem_Ioo.1 hx; nlinarith)
    have h_mono2 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Ici 1) :=
      strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Ici _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
        rw [(f_deriv x).deriv]; have : 1 < x := Set.mem_Ioi.1 hx; nlinarith)

    have f0 : f 0 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
    have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
    have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
    have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num

    have hb_bound : 1/3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
      constructor
      · by_contra! h; have a_lt : a < 1/3 := by linarith [h₀.1]
        have fa_lt : f a < f (1/3) := h_mono1 a_lt.le (le_refl _) a_lt
        have fb_lt : f b < f (1/3) := h_mono1 h.le (le_refl _) h
        have : f a = k ∧ f b = k := ⟨hf_k a (.inl rfl), hf_k b (.inr (.inl rfl))⟩
        nlinarith [this.1, this.2, f13, hk.2]
      · by_contra! h; have c_gt : 1 < c := by linarith [h₀.2]
        have fb_gt : f b > f 1 := h_mono2 (le_refl _) h.le h
        have fc_gt : f c > f 1 := h_mono2 (le_refl _) c_gt.le c_gt
        have : f b = k ∧ f c = k := ⟨hf_k b (.inr (.inl rfl)), hf_k c (.inr (.inr rfl))⟩
        nlinarith [this.1, this.2, f1, hk.1]

    repeat' constructor
    · exact h_mono1.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by linarith)) (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by norm_num)) |>.mpr (by rw [hf_k a (.inl rfl), f0]; exact hk.1)
    · linarith [h₀.1, hb_bound.1]
    · exact hb_bound.1
    · exact hb_bound.2
    · linarith [h₀.2, hb_bound.2]
    · exact h_mono2.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (le_refl _)) (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (by linarith)) |>.mp (by rw [hf_k c (.inr (.inr rfl)), f43]; exact hk.2)
```<think>
[The proof uses the polynomial $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$, where $k = abc$. The roots are $a, b, c$. The derivative $P'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1$ has roots $1/3$ and $1$. Monotonicity of $P$ on $(-\infty, 1/3]$, $[1/3, 1]$, and $[1, \infty)$ combined with $P(a)=P(b)=P(c)=0$ and the discriminant condition $0 \leq k \leq 4/27$ (derived from the non-negativity of the discriminant of a cubic with real roots) allows us to locate $a, b, c$ in the specified intervals. We use `StrictMonoOn.le_iff_le` to handle the endpoint evaluations.]
</think>

import Mathlib
import Aesop

set_option maxHeartbeats 0

open BigOperators Real Nat Rat Finset Topology

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
  let k := a * b * c
  have h_root (x : ℝ) (hx : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c) : f x = k := by
    dsimp [f]
    have : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a + b + c) * x^2 + (a * b + b * c + c * a) * x - a * b * c := by ring
    have h_zero : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = 0 := by rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp
    rw [h_zero, h₁, h₂] at this
    linarith

  have ha : f a = k := h_root a (.inl rfl)
  have hb_val : f b = k := h_root b (.inr (.inl rfl))
  have hc : f c = k := h_root c (.inr (.inr rfl))

  have h_disc : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by
    have : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = (a+b+c)^2*(a*b+b*c+c*a)^2 - 4*(a*b+b*c+c*a)^3 - 4*(a+b+c)^3*(a*b*c) + 18*(a+b+c)*(a*b+b*c+c*a)*(a*b*c) - 27*(a*b*c)^2 := by ring
    rw [this, h₁, h₂]
    ring

  have hk_range : 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 4 / 27 := by
    have h_pos : 0 ≤ -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by rw [← h_disc]; positivity
    constructor
    · nlinarith [h_pos]
    · nlinarith [h_pos]

  have f_deriv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt f ((3 * x - 1) * (x - 1)) x := by
    intro x; dsimp [f]
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun x => x^3) (3 * x^2) x := hasDerivAt_pow 3 x
    have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun x => 2 * x^2) (4 * x) x := by
      have := hasDerivAt_pow 2 x
      simpa using HasDerivAt.const_mul 2 this
    have h3 : HasDerivAt (fun x => x) 1 x := hasDerivAt_id x
    convert HasDerivAt.add (HasDerivAt.sub h1 h2) h3 using 1
    ring

  have f_cont : Continuous f := by continuity

  have h_mono1 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Iic (1/3)) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Iic _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
      let d := (f_deriv x).deriv
      have : x < 1/3 := Set.mem_Iio.1 hx
      have : d = (3*x - 1)*(x - 1) := HasDerivAt.deriv (f_deriv x)
      rw [this]; nlinarith)

  have h_anti : StrictAntiOn f (Set.Icc (1/3) 1) :=
    strictAntiOn_of_deriv_neg (convex_Icc _ _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
      let d := (f_deriv x).deriv
      have hx' : 1/3 < x ∧ x < 1 := Set.mem_Ioo.1 hx
      have : d = (3*x - 1)*(x - 1) := HasDerivAt.deriv (f_deriv x)
      rw [this]; nlinarith)

  have h_mono2 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Ici 1) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Ici _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
      let d := (f_deriv x).deriv
      have : 1 < x := Set.mem_Ioi.1 hx
      have : d = (3*x - 1)*(x - 1) := HasDerivAt.deriv (f_deriv x)
      rw [this]; nlinarith)

  have f0 : f 0 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num

  have hb : 1/3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
    constructor
    · by_contra! h; have : a < 1/3 := by linarith [h₀.1]
      have : f a < f (1/3) := h_mono1 this.le (le_refl _) this
      have : f b < f (1/3) := h_mono1 h.le (le_refl _) h
      nlinarith [ha, hb_val, f13, hk_range.2]
    · by_contra! h; have : 1 < c := by linarith [h₀.2]
      have : f b > f 1 := h_mono2 (le_refl _) h.le h
      have : f c > f 1 := h_mono2 (le_refl _) this.le this
      nlinarith [hb_val, hc, f1, hk_range.1]

  repeat' constructor
  · exact h_mono1.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by linarith)) (Set.mem_Iic.mpr (by norm_num)) |>.mpr (by rw [ha, f0]; exact hk_range.1)
  · linarith [h₀.1, hb.1]
  · exact hb.1
  · exact hb.2
  · linarith [h₀.2, hb.2]
  · exact h_mono2.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (le_refl _)) (Set.mem_Ici.mpr (by linarith)) |>.mp (by rw [hc, f43]; exact hk_range.2)
```<think>
The goal is to prove the bounds for $a, b, c$ given $a \le b \le c$, $a+b+c=2$, and $ab+bc+ca=1$.
These conditions imply that $a, b, c$ are roots of the cubic $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$, where $k = abc$.
Let $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x = x(x-1)^2$. The roots satisfy $f(x) = k$.
The derivative $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$ has zeros at $1/3$ and $1$.
$f(0) = 0, f(1/3) = 4/27, f(1) = 0, f(4/3) = 4/27$.
The discriminant of the cubic $x^3 + px^2 + qx + r$ is $\Delta = -4q^3 + p^2q^2 - 4p^3r + 18pqr - 27r^2$.
Here $p = -2, q = 1, r = -k$.
$\Delta = -4(1)^3 + (-2)^2(1)^2 - 4(-2)^3(-k) + 18(-2)(1)(-k) - 27(-k)^2 = -4 + 4 - 32k + 36k - 27k^2 = 4k - 27k^2$.
For real roots, $\Delta \ge 0 \implies 0 \le k \le 4/27$.
The behavior of $f(x)$ on intervals:
- $[0, 1/3]$: $f$ increases from $0$ to $4/27$.
- $[1/3, 1]$: $f$ decreases from $4/27$ to $0$.
- $[1, \infty)$: $f$ increases from $0$.
Since $f(a)=f(b)=f(c)=k$ and $a \le b \le c$, $a$ must be in the first part, $b$ in the second, and $c$ in the third.
Specifically: $a \in [0, 1/3]$, $b \in [1/3, 1]$, $c \in [1, 4/3]$ because $f(4/3)=4/27$.
I will use `deriv` and monotonicity.
</think>

    have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
    have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
    have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num

    · exact h_mono1.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨le_refl _, by norm_num⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨(by linarith), (by linarith [h₀.1, hb.1])⟩) |>.mpr (by rw [f0, ha]; exact hk₀)

The goal is to prove $0 \le a \le 1/3 \le b \le 1 \le c \le 4/3$ given $a \le b \le c$, $a+b+c=2$, and $ab+bc+ca=1$.
These conditions imply $a, b, c$ are roots of $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k = 0$ where $k = abc$.
Let $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$. Then $f(a) = f(b) = f(c) = k$.
The derivative $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$ has zeros at $1/3$ and $1$.
The local maximum of $f$ is $f(1/3) = 4/27$, and the local minimum is $f(1) = 0$.
For $f(x)=k$ to have three real roots $a \le b \le c$, we must have $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
By analyzing the monotonicity of $f$:
- $f$ increases on $(-\infty, 1/3]$ from $-\infty$ to $4/27$. Since $f(0)=0$ and $f(a)=k \in [0, 4/27]$, we have $0 \le a \le 1/3$.
- $f$ decreases on $[1/3, 1]$ from $4/27$ to $0$. Since $f(b)=k \in [0, 4/27]$, we have $1/3 \le b \le 1$.
- $f$ increases on $[1, \infty)$ from $0$ to $\infty$. Since $f(c)=k \in [0, 4/27]$ and $f(4/3)=4/27$, we have $1 \le c \le 4/3$.

I will use `polyrith` or manual `ring` expansion for the discriminant and `strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos` for monotonicity.

    have h_poly : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a + b + c) * x^2 + (a * b + b * c + c * a) * x - a * b * c := by ring
    rcases hx with (rfl | rfl | rfl)
    all_goals
      simp at h_poly
      rw [h₁, h₂] at h_poly
      dsimp [f]
      linarith
  
  have ha : f a = k := h_root a (by simp)
  have hb_root : f b = k := h_root b (by simp)
  have hc : f c = k := h_root c (by simp)

      _ = (a+b+c)^2*(a*b+b*c+c*a)^2 - 4*(a*b+b*c+c*a)^3 - 4*(a+b+c)^3*(a*b*c) + 18*(a+b+c)*(a*b+b*c+c*a)*(a*b*c) - 27*(a*b*c)^2 := by ring

      _ = -27 * k^2 + 4 * k := by ring

    · nlinarith [h_disc_ge]
    · nlinarith [h_disc_ge]

The goal is to prove bounds for the roots $a \le b \le c$ of the cubic $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c)$.
From $h_1, h_2$, we have $P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$ where $k = abc$.
The discriminant $\Delta = (a-b)^2(b-c)^2(c-a)^2$ must be non-negative.
Calculating $\Delta$ in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials $s_1=2, s_2=1, s_3=k$:
$\Delta = -27k^2 + 4s_1^3k - s_1^2s_2^2 + 4s_2^3 - 18s_1s_2k$.
Substituting values: $\Delta = -27k^2 + 4(8)k - 4(1)^2 + 4(1)^3 - 18(2)(1)k = -27k^2 + 32k - 4 + 4 - 36k = -27k^2 + 4k - 4$ is wrong. Let's recompute.
$\Delta = s_1^2 s_2^2 - 4 s_2^3 - 4 s_1^3 k + 18 s_1 s_2 k - 27 k^2 = (4)(1) - 4(1) - 4(8)k + 18(2)(1)k - 27k^2 = -32k + 36k - 27k^2 = 4k - 27k^2$.
So $4k - 27k^2 \ge 0 \implies 0 \le k \le 4/27$.
The function $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$ has $f(a)=f(b)=f(c)=k$.
$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$. Roots are $1/3, 1$.
$f(0)=0, f(1/3)=4/27, f(1)=0, f(4/3)=4/27$.
Since $f(a)=k \in [0, 4/27]$ and $a$ is the smallest root, $a \in [0, 1/3]$.
Since $f(b)=k$ and $b$ is the middle root, $b \in [1/3, 1]$.
Since $f(c)=k$ and $c$ is the largest root, $c \in [1, 4/3]$.

import Mathlib
import Aesop

open BigOperators Real Nat Rat Finset Topology

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x
  let k := a * b * c
  have h_root (x : ℝ) (hx : x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c) : f x = k := by
    have : (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a + b + c) * x^2 + (a * b + b * c + c * a) * x - a * b * c := by ring
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl
    all_goals (rw [h₁, h₂] at this; dsimp [f]; linarith)

  have ha : f a = k := h_root a (.inl rfl)
  have hb : f b = k := h_root b (.inr (.inl rfl))
  have hc : f c = k := h_root c (.inr (.inr rfl))

  have h_disc : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = 4 * k - 27 * k^2 := by
    let s1 := a + b + c
    let s2 := a * b + b * c + c * a
    let s3 := a * b * c
    have : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = s1^2 * s2^2 - 4 * s2^3 - 4 * s1^3 * s3 + 18 * s1 * s2 * s3 - 27 * s3^2 := by ring
    rw [this]; change s1 with 2 at *; change s2 with 1 at *; change s3 with k at *; ring

  have hk : 0 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ 4 / 27 := by
    have h_disc_pos : 0 ≤ 4 * k - 27 * k^2 := by rw [← h_disc]; positivity
    constructor
    · nlinarith [h_disc_pos]
    · nlinarith [h_disc_pos]

  have f_deriv (x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt f ((3 * x - 1) * (x - 1)) x := by
    dsimp [f]; convert (((hasDerivAt_pow 3 x).sub (HasDerivAt.const_mul 2 (hasDerivAt_pow 2 x))).add (hasDerivAt_id x)) using 1; ring

  have f_cont : Continuous f := by continuity
  have f0 : f 0 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f13 : f (1/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num
  have f1 : f 1 = 0 := by dsimp [f]; ring
  have f43 : f (4/3) = 4/27 := by dsimp [f]; norm_num

  have h_mono1 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Icc 0 (1/3)) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Icc _ _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
      rw [(f_deriv x).deriv]; rcases Set.mem_Ioo.1 hx with ⟨hx1, hx2⟩; nlinarith)
  have h_anti : StrictAntiOn f (Set.Icc (1/3) 1) :=
    strictAntiOn_of_deriv_neg (convex_Icc _ _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
      rw [(f_deriv x).deriv]; rcases Set.mem_Ioo.1 hx with ⟨hx1, hx2⟩; nlinarith)
  have h_mono2 : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Icc 1 (4/3)) :=
    strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Icc _ _) f_cont.continuousOn (fun x hx => by
      rw [(f_deriv x).deriv]; rcases Set.mem_Ioo.1 hx with ⟨hx1, hx2⟩; nlinarith)

  have hb_range : 1/3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
    constructor
    · by_contra! h; have ha_lt : a < 1/3 := by linarith [h₀.1]
      have : f b < 4/27 := by
        cases' le_or_lt 0 b with b0 b0
        · rw [← f13]; exact h_mono1 (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨b0, h.le⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num⟩) h
        · dsimp [f]; nlinarith
      nlinarith [hb, hk.2]
    · by_contra! h; have hc_gt : 1 < c := by linarith [h₀.2]
      have : f b < 0 := by
        cases' le_or_lt b (4/3) with b43 b43
        · rw [← f1]; exact h_anti (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by norm_num, h.le⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num⟩) h
        · have : f b > 4/27 := by rw [← f43]; exact h_mono2 (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by linarith, b43.le⟩) b43
          nlinarith
      nlinarith [hb, hk.1]

  repeat' constructor
  · exact (h_mono1.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨le_refl 0, by norm_num⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by linarith [h₀.1, hb_range.1], by linarith [h₀.1, hb_range.1]⟩)).2 (by rw [f0, ha]; exact hk.1)
  · exact (h_mono1.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num⟩)).2 (by rw [ha, f13]; exact hk.2)
  · exact hb_range.1
  · exact hb_range.2
  · exact (h_mono2.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by linarith [h₀.2, hb_range.2], by linarith [h₀.2, hb_range.2]⟩)).2 (by rw [f1, hc]; exact hk.1)
  · exact (h_mono2.le_iff_le (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩) (Set.mem_Icc.2 ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num⟩)).2 (by rw [hc, f43]; exact hk.2)

To decompose the goal into intermediate leaf obligations, we first recognize that $a, b, c$ are roots of the cubic polynomial $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - (a+b+c)x^2 + (ab+bc+ca)x - abc$.
Given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$, we have $P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc = x(x-1)^2 - abc$.
Let $k = abc$. The condition that $a, b, c$ are real roots and $a \le b \le c$ implies constraints on $k$ based on the local extrema of $f(x) = x(x-1)^2$.
The derivative $f'(x) = (x-1)^2 + 2x(x-1) = (x-1)(3x-1)$ shows local maximum at $1/3$ and local minimum at $1$.
Specifically, $f(1/3) = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$ and $f(1) = 0$.
For three real roots to exist, we must have $0 \le abc \le 4/27$.
The roots $a, b, c$ will then lie in the intervals determined by these extrema: $a \in [0, 1/3]$, $b \in [1/3, 1]$, and $c \in [1, 4/3]$ (since $c \le a+b+c = 2$ and more precisely $f(4/3) = 4/27 \ge k$).

I will decompose this into:
1. $a, b, c$ are roots of $x(x-1)^2 = abc$.
2. The range of $abc$ is $[0, 4/27]$.
3. Monotonicity/root location properties of $x(x-1)^2 - k$.
</think>

The objective is to prove the identity `(x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x * (x - 1)^2 - a * b * c` given the conditions `a + b + c = 2` and `a * b + b * c + c * a = 1`.

1. Expand the left side:
   `(x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - (a + b + c)x^2 + (ab + bc + ca)x - abc`.

2. Substitute the given conditions:
   `a + b + c = 2` and `ab + bc + ca = 1`.
   So, `(x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc`.

3. Expand the right side (excluding `abc`):
   `x * (x - 1)^2 = x * (x^2 - 2x + 1) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x`.

4. Comparing the two expressions:
   The left side is `(x^3 - 2x^2 + x) - abc`.
   The right side is `x * (x - 1)^2 - abc`.
   Since `x^3 - 2x^2 + x = x * (x - 1)^2`, the identity holds.

I will use `ring` to verify this algebraic identity after substituting the constants.

The goal is to prove $0 \le abc \le 4/27$ given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$, with $a \le b \le c$.
The polynomial $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc$ has roots $a, b, c$.
Let $k = abc$. Then $P(x) = x(x-1)^2 - k$.
Since $a, b, c$ are roots, $k = a(a-1)^2 = b(b-1)^2 = c(c-1)^2$.
For $x(x-1)^2 = k$ to have three real roots, $k$ must be between the local minimum and maximum of $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$.
$g'(x) = (x-1)^2 + 2x(x-1) = (x-1)(x-1+2x) = (x-1)(3x-1)$.
Extreme points are at $x=1$ (local min, $g(1)=0$) and $x=1/3$ (local max, $g(1/3) = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$).
Since $a, b, c$ are real, $k$ must lie in $[0, 4/27]$.
Thus $0 \le abc \le 4/27$.
I will use the properties of the roots and the derivative of $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ to bound $abc$.
Actually, I can just use the fact that $g(a) = g(b) = g(c) = abc$.
Since $g(x) \ge 0$ for $x \ge 0$, and we can show $a \ge 0$ (if $a < 0$, then $g(a) < 0$, but $k \ge 0$ because $g(x)$ for $x \in [b, c]$ must be positive).
Wait, $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$. $g(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \ge 0$.
If $k < 0$, then $x(x-1)^2 = k$ has only one real root (at $x < 0$). But we have 3 roots. So $k \ge 0$.
The maximum value of $x(x-1)^2$ on $[0, 1]$ is $4/27$ at $x=1/3$.
Since there are roots in $[0, 1]$ and $[1, \infty)$, and $g(x)$ reaches $k$ three times, $k$ must be $\le \max_{x \in [0, 1]} g(x) = 4/27$.
Actually, a more direct way: the discriminant of $x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$ must be $\ge 0$.
$\Delta = -4(-2)^3(-k) + (-2)^2(1)^2 - 4(1)^3 - 27(-k)^2 + 18(-2)(1)(-k)$.
$\Delta = -32k + 4 - 4 - 27k^2 + 36k = 4k - 27k^2 = k(4 - 27k)$.
$\Delta \ge 0 \iff k(4-27k) \ge 0 \iff 0 \le k \le 4/27$.
This is perfect.

        use [a, b, c]; simp [h₀.1, h₀.2])

      have h_P_coeffs : P = Polynomial.C 1 * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C a) * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C b) * (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C c) := by

To show $0 \le abc \le 4/27$, we analyze the polynomial $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$.
The condition $a, b, c$ being the roots of $f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - k = 0$ (where $k=abc$) implies that $k$ must be a value attained by $g(x)$ such that it has three real roots $a \le b \le c$.
$g'(x) = (x-1)^2 + 2x(x-1) = (x-1)(x-1+2x) = (x-1)(3x-1)$.
The local maximum of $g(x)$ is at $x=1/3$, where $g(1/3) = (1/3)(1 - 1/3)^2 = (1/3)(4/9) = 4/27$.
The local minimum is at $x=1$, where $g(1) = 0$.
For $g(x) - k = 0$ to have three real roots, $k$ must lie between the local minimum and local maximum values of $g(x)$.
Thus $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
In the proof, we use the fact that if $a, b, c$ are roots of $x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k = 0$, then $k$ is bounded by the values of the function at its critical points.
Since $a \le b \le c$, the discriminant of the cubic must be non-negative.
Alternatively, $k = g(a) = g(b) = g(c)$. Since $g(x) \to -\infty$ for $x \to -\infty$ and $g(x) \to \infty$ for $x \to \infty$, and we have 3 roots, $k$ must be in the range $[g(1), g(1/3)] = [0, 4/27]$.
Specifically, for $x \in [0, 1]$, $g(x) \ge 0$. Since $a, b, c$ are real roots and $a+b+c=2, ab+bc+ca=1$, we know $k = abc$ and the roots satisfy $g(x)=k$.
The maximum value of $x(x-1)^2$ on $[0, 1]$ is $4/27$.
Also $a(a-1)^2 = k$. Since $a \le b \le c$ and their sum is 2, and $ab+bc+ca=1$, the derivative check ensures $k \in [0, 4/27]$.

The goal is to prove $0 \le abc \le 4/27$ given $a+b+c=2$, $ab+bc+ca=1$, and $a \le b \le c$.
The polynomial $(x-a)(x-b)(x-c)$ expands to $x^3 - (a+b+c)x^2 + (ab+bc+ca)x - abc = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc$.
Let $f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x = x(x-1)^2$. Then $f(a) = f(b) = f(c) = abc$.
By Rolle's Theorem, there exist $x_1 \in [a, b]$ and $x_2 \in [b, c]$ such that $f'(x_1) = 0$ and $f'(x_2) = 0$.
$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$. The roots are $1/3$ and $1$.
Since $a \le b \le c$, and $x_1, x_2$ are distinct or if $a=b=c$ then $x_1=x_2$, the critical points $1/3$ and $1$ must lie within $[a, c]$.
The values of $f$ at the critical points are $f(1/3) = (1/3)(1/3-1)^2 = (1/3)(4/9) = 4/27$ and $f(1) = 0$.
For the equation $f(x) = k$ to have three real roots $a, b, c$, the constant $k$ must lie between the local minimum and local maximum.
Thus $0 \le abc \le 4/27$.

I will use `exists_deriv_eq_zero` and basic calculus properties to show that the value $abc$ must be between the local extrema of $f(x) = x(x-1)^2$.
Specifically, $f(1)=0$ is a local minimum and $f(1/3)=4/27$ is a local maximum.
Since $f(a)=f(b)=f(c)=abc$, Rolle's theorem gives critical points in $[a,b]$ and $[b,c]$.
The only critical points are $1/3$ and $1$.
If $a < b < c$, then $x_1 \in (a, b)$ and $x_2 \in (b, c)$ are distinct, so $\{x_1, x_2\} = \{1/3, 1\}$.
In any case $abc$ must be in the interval $[f(1), f(1/3)] = [0, 4/27]$.

  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :

      have h_abc : f a = a * b * c ∧ f b = a * b * c ∧ f c = a * b * c := by
        constructor; · rw [← sub_eq_zero, h_f_eq]; ring
        constructor; · rw [← sub_eq_zero, h_f_eq]; ring
        · rw [← sub_eq_zero, h_f_eq]; ring

            rw [hx2] at hx2_mem; have fk := h_abc.2.1; rw [← fk];

import Mathlib
import Aesop

set_option maxHeartbeats 0

open BigOperators Real Nat Rat Finset Topology

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  
    -- Let f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc
    -- Then f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - abc
    -- Let k = abc. The roots of x(x-1)^2 = k are a, b, c.
  
    have h_poly : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x * (x - 1)^2 - a * b * c := by
      admit
  
    have h_k_range : 0 ≤ a * b * c ∧ a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x * (x - 1)^2
      have hf : ∀ x, f x - a * b * c = (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) := by
        intro x; rw [← h_poly x]; ring
      have ha : f a = a * b * c := by linarith [hf a]
      have hb : f b = a * b * c := by linarith [hf b]
      have hc : f c = a * b * c := by linarith [hf c]
      
      -- Let P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k.
      -- The derivative is P'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1.
      -- Roots of P'(x) are 1/3 and 1.
      -- By Rolle's theorem, the roots of P'(x) must separate the roots a, b, c.
      -- If a, b, c are real, the local extrema P(1/3) and P(1) must have opposite signs or be zero.
      -- P(1/3) = f(1/3) - k = 4/27 - k
      -- P(1) = f(1) - k = 0 - k
      -- For three real roots, we must have P(1) ≤ 0 and P(1/3) ≥ 0.
      
      have h_f_deriv : ∀ x, HasDerivAt f (3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1) x := by
        intro x; show HasDerivAt (fun x => x^3 - 2*x^2 + x) _ x
        convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).pow 3).sub ((hasDerivAt_id x).pow 2).const_mul 2).add (hasDerivAt_id x)
        ring; ring
        
      have h_crit : ∀ x, 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 = 0 ↔ x = 1 ∨ x = 1/3 := by
        intro x; constructor
        · intro h; have : 3 * (x - 1) * (x - 1/3) = 0 := by ring_nf; linarith
          rcases mul_eq_zero.mp this with h1 | h2; left; linarith; right; linarith
        · intro h; rcases h with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
        
      have k_nonneg : 0 ≤ a * b * c := by
        by_cases h_dist : b = c
        · rw [← hc, h_dist]; dsimp [f]; nlinarith
        · obtain ⟨x, _, hx_zero⟩ := exists_deriv_eq_zero f b c (lt_of_le_of_ne h₀.2 h_dist) 
            (fun _ _ => (h_f_deriv _).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt) (by rw [hb, hc])
          rw [h_crit x] at hx_zero
          rcases hx_zero with rfl | rfl
          · rw [← hb]; dsimp [f]; norm_num
          · have : b < 1/3 ∧ 1/3 < c := by linarith [‹x = 1/3›, ‹b < c›]
            -- This case is actually impossible under a <= b <= c given the shape, 
            -- but the value k = f(x) where f'(x)=0 handles the bounds.
            rw [← hb]; dsimp [f]; nlinarith
            
      have k_le : a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
        by_cases h_dist : a = b
        · rw [← ha, h_dist]; dsimp [f]; 
          have : a * (a - 1)^2 = (a - 1/3)^2 * (a + 4/3) * (3/3) + 4/27 := by ring -- Check if this helps
          have : 4/27 - a * (a - 1)^2 = (1 - a) * (a - 1/3)^2 := by ring
          nlinarith
        · obtain ⟨x, _, hx_zero⟩ := exists_deriv_eq_zero f a b (lt_of_le_of_ne h₀.1 h_dist)
            (fun _ _ => (h_f_deriv _).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt) (by rw [ha, hb])
          rw [h_crit x] at hx_zero
          rcases hx_zero with rfl | rfl
          · rw [← ha]; dsimp [f]; norm_num
          · rw [← ha]; dsimp [f]; norm_num
          
      exact ⟨k_nonneg, k_le⟩
  
    have h_a_bounds : 0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 := by
      admit
  
    have h_b_bounds : 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
      admit
  
    have h_c_bounds : 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
      admit
  
    exact ⟨h_a_bounds.1, h_a_bounds.2, h_b_bounds.1, h_b_bounds.2, h_c_bounds.1, h_c_bounds.2⟩

The goal is to prove $0 \le abc \le 4/27$ given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$.
This corresponds to finding the range of the constant term $k$ such that the cubic $f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - k$ has three real roots $a, b, c$.
The function $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ has local extrema.
$g'(x) = (x-1)^2 + 2x(x-1) = (x-1)(x-1+2x) = (x-1)(3x-1)$.
Critical points are $x=1$ and $x=1/3$.
$g(1) = 0$.
$g(1/3) = (1/3)(1 - 1/3)^2 = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
For $g(x) = k$ to have three real roots, $k$ must be between the local minimum and the local maximum.
Thus $0 \le abc \le 4/27$.

I will decompose this into:
1. Finding the local maximum of $x(x-1)^2$.
2. Using the fact that for the cubic to have three real roots, the constant term must lie between the local extrema.
3. Establishing the specific bounds.

To prove `0 ≤ a * b * c`, we use the identity $f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x(x-1)^2 - abc$.
Substituting $x=0$, we get $(0-a)(0-b)(0-c) = 0(0-1)^2 - abc$, which simplifies to $-abc = -abc$. This doesn't help directly.
However, note that $a, b, c$ are the roots of $x(x-1)^2 = k$, where $k = abc$.
For the polynomial $P(x) = x(x-1)^2$ to have three real roots $a \le b \le c$, we must have $k$ in the range of the local extrema of $P(x)$.
$P(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$.
$P'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$.
Local maximum at $x=1/3$ is $P(1/3) = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
Local minimum at $x=1$ is $P(1) = 0$.
For three real roots, we must have $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
Thus $0 \le abc$.
Specifically, if $k < 0$, then $x(x-1)^2 = k$ implies $x < 0$ (since $(x-1)^2 \ge 0$). Thus $a < 0$.
But we need to show $abc \ge 0$.
If $abc < 0$, then since $(x-1)^2 \ge 0$, $x(x-1)^2 = abc$ implies $x < 0$.
This means all three roots $a, b, c$ must be negative.
But $a+b+c=2$, which contradicts $a, b, c < 0$.
Therefore, $abc$ cannot be negative.
Thus $abc \ge 0$.

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  -- Let f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc
  -- Then f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - abc
  -- Let k = abc. The roots of x(x-1)^2 = k are a, b, c.
  
  have h_poly : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x * (x - 1)^2 - a * b * c := by
    admit
  
  have h_k_range : 0 ≤ a * b * c ∧ a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
    have h_abc_nonneg : 0 ≤ a * b * c := by
      let k := a * b * c
      have h_at_0 := h_poly 0
      simp only [sub_zero, zero_sub, neg_mul, neg_neg] at h_at_0
      -- Since a+b+c = 2 and ab+bc+ca = 1, if k < 0, 
      -- then x(x-1)^2 = k has only one real root which is negative.
      -- But a+b+c=2 > 0 implies at least one root is positive.
      by_contra h_neg
      have h_k_lt_0 : k < 0 := not_le.mp h_neg
      have h_root : ∀ x, x * (x - 1)^2 = k → x < 0 := by
        intro x hx
        have h_sq_nonneg : 0 ≤ (x - 1)^2 := sq_nonneg (x - 1)
        if h_sq_zero : (x - 1)^2 = 0 then
          rw [h_sq_zero, mul_zero] at hx
          exact (lt_irrefl 0 (hx ▸ h_k_lt_0)).elim
        else
          have h_sq_pos : 0 < (x - 1)^2 := (ne_iff_lt_or_gt.mp h_sq_zero).elim (lambda h => (sq_nonneg (x-1)).lt_of_ne (Ne.symm h_sq_zero)) (lambda h => h)
          exact pos_and_neg_product_is_neg hx h_sq_pos
      have ha : a < 0 := h_root a (by rw [← h_at_0]; simp [h_poly])
      have hb : b < 0 := h_root b (by rw [← h_at_0]; simp [h_poly])
      have hc : c < 0 := h_root c (by rw [← h_at_0]; simp [h_poly])
      linarith
    have h_abc_upper : a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      admit
    exact ⟨h_abc_nonneg, h_abc_upper⟩

    admit
  
  have h_b_bounds : 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
    admit
  
  have h_c_bounds : 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
    admit

To prove $0 \leq abc$ given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$, we use the characteristic polynomial $f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc$. Since $a, b, c$ are real roots, the local maximum of $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ must be at least $abc$. The roots of $g'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0$ are $x = 1$ and $x = 1/3$. 
The local minimum of $g(x)$ is $g(1) = 0$. Since $a \le b \le c$ are roots of $g(x) = abc$, and the minimum value of $g(x)$ between its local extrema is $0$, we must have $abc \ge 0$. Specifically, $g(x) \ge 0$ for $x \ge 0$, and since $g(x)$ has 3 non-negative roots only if $abc \ge 0$. More formally, $a^2+b^2+c^2 = (a+b+c)^2 - 2(ab+bc+ca) = 4 - 2 = 2$.
Consider $a, b, c$ as roots of $t^3 - 2t^2 + t - k = 0$ where $k = abc$. 
$f(t) = t(t-1)^2 - k$. For $f(t)$ to have three real roots, the value $k$ must lie between the local minimum and local maximum of $g(t) = t(t-1)^2$.
$g'(t) = (t-1)^2 + 2t(t-1) = (t-1)(t-1+2t) = (t-1)(3t-1)$.
Local max at $t=1/3$ is $g(1/3) = 1/3(2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
Local min at $t=1$ is $g(1) = 0$.
Thus $0 \le k \le 4/27$.

To show $0 \leq abc$, we use the fact that $a, b, c$ are the roots of the cubic polynomial $f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$, where $k = abc$.
This can be written as $f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - k$.
Since $a \le b \le c$ are real roots, $k$ must be a value attained by the function $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ such that it has three real roots.
The local extrema of $g(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$ are found by $g'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0$, which gives $x = 1$ and $x = 1/3$.
$g(1) = 0$ and $g(1/3) = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
For $g(x) = k$ to have three real roots, $k$ must lie in the range $[g(1), g(1/3)]$, i.e., $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
Thus $abc \ge 0$.
Specifically, if $abc < 0$, then $g(x) = abc$ would have only one real root (since $g(x) \to -\infty$ as $x \to -\infty$ and the local minimum is $0$), but we have three real roots.
Alternatively, since $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$, if $x < 0$, then $g(x) < 0$. If $k < 0$, then $g(x) = k$ has one root $x < 0$. But if $a < 0$, then $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$ implies $b+c = 2-a$ and $bc = 1 - a(b+c) = 1 - a(2-a) = 1 - 2a + a^2 = (1-a)^2$.
Then $(b-c)^2 = (b+c)^2 - 4bc = (2-a)^2 - 4(1-a)^2 = (2-a-2+2a)(2-a+2-2a) = a(4-3a)$.
For $b, c$ to be real, $a(4-3a) \ge 0$, which means $0 \le a \le 4/3$. Thus $a$ cannot be negative.
Since $a \le b \le c$, if $a \ge 0$, then $abc \ge 0$.

        exact (mul_neg_iff.mp this).resolve_right (fun h => (not_le.mpr h.2) (sq_nonneg (a - 1)))
      have h_bc_prod : b * c = 1 - a * (b + c) := by rw [← h₂]; ring
      have h_bc_sum : b + c = 2 - a := by linarith
      have h_discr : (b - c)^2 = a * (3 * a - 4) := by
        have : (b - c)^2 = (b + c)^2 - 4 * (b * c) := by ring
        rw [h_bc_sum, h_bc_prod, h_bc_sum] at this
        ring_nf at this ⊢
        exact this
      have h_sq_nonneg : 0 ≤ (b - c)^2 := sq_nonneg (b - c)
      rw [h_discr] at h_sq_nonneg
      have h_3a_4_neg : 3 * a - 4 < 0 := by linarith
      have h_prod_pos : a * (3 * a - 4) > 0 := mul_pos_of_neg_of_neg h_a_neg h_3a_4_neg
      exact (not_le.mpr h_prod_pos) h_sq_nonneg
    have h_abc_upper : a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      admit
    exact ⟨h_abc_nonneg, h_abc_upper⟩
    
  
  have h_a_bounds : 0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 := by
    admit
  
  have h_b_bounds : 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
    admit
  
  have h_c_bounds : 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
    admit
  
  exact ⟨h_a_bounds.1, h_a_bounds.2, h_b_bounds.1, h_b_bounds.2, h_c_bounds.1, h_c_bounds.2⟩
```<think>
To show $0 \le abc$, we use the fact that $b, c$ are roots of a quadratic.
Given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$:
$b+c = 2-a$ and $bc = 1-a(b+c) = 1-a(2-a) = a^2-2a+1 = (a-1)^2$.
For $b, c$ to be real, the discriminant of $x^2 - (2-a)x + (a-1)^2 = 0$ must be non-negative.
$D = (2-a)^2 - 4(a-1)^2 = (2-a-2a+2)(2-a+2a-2) = (4-3a)(a) \ge 0$.
Thus $a(4-3a) \ge 0$.
Since $a \le b \le c$, and $a+b+c=2$, $3a \le a+b+c = 2$, so $a \le 2/3$.
Then $4-3a \ge 4-2 = 2 > 0$.
From $a(4-3a) \ge 0$, we must have $a \ge 0$.
Since $bc = (a-1)^2 \ge 0$ and $a \ge 0$, we have $abc \ge 0$.

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  -- Let f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc
  -- Then f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - abc
  -- Let k = abc. The roots of x(x-1)^2 = k are a, b, c.
  
  have h_poly : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x * (x - 1)^2 - a * b * c := by
    admit
  
  have h_k_range : 0 ≤ a * b * c ∧ a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
    have h_abc_nonneg : 0 ≤ a * b * c := by
      have h_bc : b * c = (a - 1)^2 := by
        have : b * c = 1 - a * (b + c) := by rw [← h₂]; ring
        have : b + c = 2 - a := by linarith
        rw [‹b + c = 2 - a›] at ‹b * c = 1 - a * (b + c)›
        rw [‹b * c = 1 - a * (2 - a)›]
        ring
      have h_disc : 0 ≤ (b - c)^2 := sq_nonneg (b - c)
      have : (b - c)^2 = (b + c)^2 - 4 * (b * c) := by ring
      have h_sum : b + c = 2 - a := by linarith
      rw [h_sum, h_bc] at this
      have h_abc_expr : (2 - a)^2 - 4 * (a - 1)^2 = a * (4 - 3 * a) := by ring
      rw [h_abc_expr] at this
      rw [this] at h_disc
      have h_a_le_23 : a ≤ 2 / 3 := by linarith
      have h_43a_pos : 0 < 4 - 3 * a := by linarith
      have h_a_nonneg : 0 ≤ a := (mul_nonneg_iff_of_pos_right h_43a_pos).mp h_disc
      rw [h_bc]
      exact mul_nonneg h_a_nonneg (sq_nonneg (a - 1))
    have h_abc_upper : a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      admit

To prove $0 \le abc$, we use the equations $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$.
Express $b$ and $c$ in terms of $a$:

To show $abc \le 4/27$ given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$, we consider the polynomial $f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc$.
Let $g(x) = x(x-1)^2 = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$. Then $f(x) = g(x) - abc$.
Since $a, b, c$ are the roots of $f(x)$, $abc$ must be a value such that $g(x) = abc$ has three real roots.
The local extrema of $g(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$ occur where $g'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0$.
The roots of $3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1) = 0$ are $x = 1/3$ and $x = 1$.
The local maximum value is $g(1/3) = (1/3)(1 - 1/3)^2 = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
The local minimum value is $g(1) = 1(1-1)^2 = 0$.
For $g(x) = abc$ to have three real roots, $abc$ must lie in the range $[g(1), g(1/3)]$, i.e., $0 \le abc \le 4/27$.
In Lean, I will use the derivative of $g(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$ and the fact that its local maximum is $4/27$.

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  -- Let f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc
  -- Then f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - abc
  -- Let k = abc. The roots of x(x-1)^2 = k are a, b, c.
  
  have h_poly : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x * (x - 1)^2 - a * b * c := by
    admit
  
  have h_k_range : 0 ≤ a * b * c ∧ a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
    have h_abc_nonneg : 0 ≤ a * b * c := by
      admit
    have h_abc_upper : a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      let g (x : ℝ) := x * (x - 1)^2
      have hg : a * b * c = g b := by
        have hfb := h_poly b
        simp [sub_self, zero_mul] at hfb
        rw [hfb, sub_eq_zero]
      have h_deriv : deriv g = λ x => 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 := by
        ext x
        simp [g]; ring_nf
        set_option linter.deprecated false in
        simp [deriv_pow, deriv_id'']
        ring
      have h_crit : ∀ x, deriv g x = 0 ↔ x = 1 / 3 ∨ x = 1 := by
        intro x
        rw [h_deriv]
        constructor
        · intro hx
          have h_fact : 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 = (3 * x - 1) * (x - 1) := by ring
          rw [h_fact] at hx
          rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hx with h1 | h2
          · left; linarith
          · right; exact h2

        intro x hx
        have g_cont : ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc a c) := by
          apply Continuous.continuousOn
          continuity
        have g_diff : DifferentiableOn g (Set.Ioo a c) := by
          apply Differentiable.differentiableOn
          apply Differentiable.mul
          · apply differentiable_id
          · apply Differentiable.pow
            apply Differentiable.sub
            · apply differentiable_id
            · apply differentiable_const
        let x_max := IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn (isCompact_Icc a c) (Set.nonempty_Icc.mpr (by linarith [h₀.1, h₀.2])) g_cont

          have h_dv : deriv g xm = 0 := isLocalMax_iff_deriv_eq_zero (differentiableAt_id.mul (differentiableAt_id.sub differentiableAt_const).pow) (Ioo_mem_nhds h_int.1 h_int.2) |>.mp (IsMaxOn.isLocalMax hmax (Icc_mem_nhds h_int.1 h_int.2))

          · ring_nf; linarith

The goal is to prove `a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27` given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$.
Let $f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc$.
For the roots $a, b, c$ to be real, the cubic $f(x)$ must have three real roots.
Let $k = abc$. Then $f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - k$.
For $f(x)$ to have real roots, $k$ must lie within the range of values taken by $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ between its local minimum and maximum.
$g'(x) = (x-1)^2 + 2x(x-1) = (x-1)(x-1+2x) = (x-1)(3x-1)$.
Critical points are $x=1$ and $x=1/3$.
$g(1) = 0$.
$g(1/3) = (1/3)(1 - 1/3)^2 = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
Since $a \le b \le c$ are real roots, $k = abc$ must satisfy $0 \le k \le 4/27$ (as $g(x)$ goes from $0$ at the local min to $4/27$ at the local max).
In Lean, I can use the fact that if a cubic $x^3 - sx^2 + qx - k$ has real roots, its discriminant must be non-negative.
The discriminant of $x^3 + px + q$ is $-4p^3 - 27q^2$.
For $x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$, we can shift $x = y + 2/3$.
Alternatively, use the condition for three real roots of $x^3 + Bx^2 + Cx + D = 0$: $18BCD - 4B^3D + B^2C^2 - 4C^3 - 27D^2 \ge 0$.
Here $B = -2, C = 1, D = -k$.
$18(-2)(1)(-k) - 4(-8)(-k) + 4(1) - 4(1) - 27k^2 \ge 0$
$36k - 32k + 4 - 27k^2 \ge 0 \implies -27k^2 + 4k + 4 \ge 0$.
Wait, let's recompute.
The discriminant $\Delta$ of $ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$ is $\Delta = 18abcd - 4b^3d + b^2c^2 - 4ac^3 - 27a^2d^2$.
For $x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$:
$a=1, b=-2, c=1, d=-k$.
$\Delta = 18(1)(-2)(1)(-k) - 4(-2)^3(-k) + (-2)^2(1)^2 - 4(1)(1)^3 - 27(1)^2(-k)^2$
$\Delta = 36k - 32k + 4 - 4 - 27k^2 = 4k - 27k^2$.
For real roots, $\Delta \ge 0 \implies 4k - 27k^2 \ge 0 \implies k(4 - 27k) \ge 0$.
Since $k = abc$ is non-negative (from the other `admit`), $4 - 27k \ge 0 \implies k \le 4/27$.

theorem algebra_apbpceq2_abpbcpcaeq1_aleq1on3anbleq1ancleq4on3 (a b c : ℝ) (h₀ : a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c)
  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  -- Let f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc
  -- Then f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - abc
  -- Let k = abc. The roots of x(x-1)^2 = k are a, b, c.
  
  have h_poly : ∀ x, (x - a) * (x - b) * (x - c) = x * (x - 1)^2 - a * b * c := by
    admit
  
  have h_k_range : 0 ≤ a * b * c ∧ a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
    have h_abc_nonneg : 0 ≤ a * b * c := by
      admit
    have h_abc_upper : a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      let f : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => x * (x - 1)^2
      have h_root : ∀ x, f x = a * b * c ↔ (x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x = c) := by
        intro x
        rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← h_poly]
        simp [f]
      have h_exist : ∃ x, f x = a * b * c := ⟨a, (h_root a).mpr (Or.inl rfl)⟩
      -- The maximum value of x(x-1)^2 for x in the relevant range can be found via calculus.
      -- However, a simpler way is using AM-GM:
      -- For x(1-x)^2 to be maximized when x in [0, 1], we look at (2x)(1-x)(1-x).
      -- (2x)(1-x)(1-x) ≤ ((2x + 1-x + 1-x)/3)^3 = (2/3)^3 = 8/27.
      -- So x(1-x)^2 ≤ 4/27.
      -- Since a, b, c are real roots of f(x) = k, the horizontal line y = k must intersect y = f(x).
      -- The local maximum of f(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x is at x=1/3, f(1/3) = 4/27.
      -- The local minimum is at x=1, f(1) = 0.
      -- For there to be 3 real roots, k must be in [0, 4/27].
      let f' : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1
      have h_deriv : deriv f = f' := by
        ext x
        simp [f]
        ring
      have h_crit : ∀ x, f' x = 0 ↔ x = 1 ∨ x = 1/3 := by
        intro x
        simp [f']
        ring_nf
        constructor
        · intro h; cases' mul_eq_zero.mp (congr_arg (λ z => z / 3) h) with h1 h2
          · right; linarith
          · left; linarith
        · rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> norm_num
      -- Using the discriminant of the cubic x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k
      let k := a * b * c
      have h_disc : 4 * k - 27 * k^2 ≥ 0 := by
        let P : Polynomial ℝ := Polynomial.coeffs_to_poly [ -k, 1, -2, 1 ]
        have h_roots : (P.rootSet ℝ).Card ≥ 1 := by admit
        -- The discriminant of x^3 + px^2 + qx + r is 18pqr - 4p^3r + p^2q^2 - 4q^3 - 27r^2
        -- For x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k: 18(-2)(1)(-k) - 4(-8)(-k) + 4(1) - 4(1) - 27k^2 = 36k - 32k - 27k^2 = 4k - 27k^2
        -- Since the roots are real, disc ≥ 0.
        admit
      exact (mul_nonneg_iff.mp h_disc).resolve_right (by admit) |>.2
    exact ⟨h_abc_nonneg, h_abc_upper⟩
    
  
  have h_a_bounds : 0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 := by
    admit
  
  have h_b_bounds : 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 := by
    admit
  
  have h_c_bounds : 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
    admit
  
  exact ⟨h_a_bounds.1, h_a_bounds.2, h_b_bounds.1, h_b_bounds.2, h_c_bounds.1, h_c_bounds.2⟩

To show $abc \leq 4/27$ given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$:
1. Let $k = abc$. The roots of $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$ are $a, b, c$.
2. For these roots to be real, the local maximum of $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ must be greater than or equal to $k$.
3. $g(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$. $g'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$.
4. The local maximum occurs at $x = 1/3$.
5. $g(1/3) = (1/3)(1/3 - 1)^2 = (1/3)(-2/3)^2 = (1/3)(4/9) = 4/27$.
6. Since $a, b, c$ are real roots, we must have $k \leq g(1/3) = 4/27$.

      exact IsLocalMax._root_.admit

The objective is to prove $abc \le 4/27$ given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$ for $a \le b \le c$.
The discriminant of the cubic polynomial $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc$ must be non-negative because the roots $a, b, c$ are real.
The discriminant of $x^3 + px^2 + qx + r$ is $\Delta = 18pqr - 4p^3r + p^2q^2 - 4q^3 - 27r^2$.
For $p=-2, q=1, r=-k$ (where $k=abc$):
$\Delta = 18(-2)(1)(-k) - 4(-2)^3(-k) + (-2)^2(1)^2 - 4(1)^3 - 27(-k)^2$
$\Delta = 36k - 32k + 4 - 4 - 27k^2 = 4k - 27k^2$.
Since $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Delta \ge 0 \implies 4k - 27k^2 \ge 0$.
Given $k \ge 0$ (from $h\_abc\_nonneg$), if $k > 0$, then $4 - 27k \ge 0 \implies k \le 4/27$. If $k=0$, $0 \le 4/27$ holds.
I will use the identity $(a-b)^2(b-c)^2(c-a)^2 = 4k - 27k^2$ derived from the given sums.
The identity $(x-y)^2(y-z)^2(z-x)^2 = s_1^2s_2^2 - 4s_2^3 - 4s_1^3s_3 + 18s_1s_2s_3 - 27s_3^2$ is standard.
With $s_1=2, s_2=1, s_3=k$:
$2^2 \cdot 1^2 - 4 \cdot 1^3 - 4 \cdot 2^3 \cdot k + 18 \cdot 2 \cdot 1 \cdot k - 27k^2$
$= 4 - 4 - 32k + 36k - 27k^2 = 4k - 27k^2$.
Since $(a-b)^2(b-c)^2(c-a)^2 \ge 0$, we have $4k - 27k^2 \ge 0$.

The objective is to prove $abc \le 4/27$ given $a+b+c=2$ and $ab+bc+ca=1$ with $a \le b \le c$.
The most direct algebraic method is using the discriminant of the cubic polynomial $P(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k$, where $k = abc$.
The discriminant of $x^3 + px^2 + qx + r$ is $\Delta = 18pqr - 4p^3r + p^2q^2 - 4q^3 - 27r^2$.
For $p = -2, q = 1, r = -k$:
$\Delta = 18(-2)(1)(-k) - 4(-2)^3(-k) + (-2)^2(1)^2 - 4(1)^3 - 27(-k)^2$
$\Delta = 36k - 32k + 4 - 4 - 27k^2 = 4k - 27k^2$.
Since the roots $a, b, c$ are real, $\Delta \ge 0$.

  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
  -- Let f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x - abc
  -- Then f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - abc
  -- Let k = abc. The roots of x(x-1)^2 = k are a, b, c.

    admit

    have h_abc_nonneg : 0 ≤ a * b * c := by
      admit
    have h_abc_upper : a * b * c ≤ 4 / 27 := by
      let k := a * b * c
      have h_disc : (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 = 4 * k - 27 * k^2 := by
        rw [h₁, h₂] at *
        ring
      have h_sq_nonneg : 0 ≤ (a - b)^2 * (b - c)^2 * (c - a)^2 := by positivity
      rw [h_disc] at h_sq_nonneg
      -- 4k - 27k^2 >= 0 => k(4 - 27k) >= 0
      have h_factor : 4 * k - 27 * k^2 = k * (4 - 27 * k) := by ring
      rw [h_factor] at h_sq_nonneg
      by_cases hk : k = 0
      · rw [hk]; norm_num

        have : 0 ≤ 4 - 27 * k := (mul_nonneg_iff_right_nonneg_of_pos hk_pos).mp h_sq_nonneg
        linarith
    exact ⟨h_abc_nonneg, h_abc_upper⟩

1. $a \in [0, 1/3]$
2. $b \in [1/3, 1]$
3. $c \in [1, 4/3]$ (since $g(4/3) = (4/3)(1/3)^2 = 4/27 \ge k$)
Given $a \le b \le c$, $a$ must be the smallest root.
Since $g(0) = 0$ and $g(1/3) = 4/27$, and $g$ is increasing on $[0, 1/3]$, the smallest root $a$ of $g(x) = k$ for $k \in [0, 4/27]$ must satisfy $0 \le a \le 1/3$.
Specifically, $g(a) = k \ge 0 \implies a(a-1)^2 \ge 0 \implies a \ge 0$.
$g(a) = k \le 4/27 = g(1/3)$. Since $g$ is increasing on $[0, 1/3]$, $a \le 1/3$.

  (h₁ : a + b + c = 2) (h₂ : a * b + b * c + c * a = 1) :
  0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3 ∧ 1 / 3 ≤ b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by

The objective is to prove `0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3` given the context.
We are given:
- `a ≤ b ∧ b ≤ c`
- `a + b + c = 2`
- `ab + bc + ca = 1`
- `f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x(x-1)^2 - k` where `k = abc`.
- `k` is in the range `[0, 4/27]`.

Roots of `f(x) = 0` are `a, b, c`.
So `a, b, c` are solutions to `x(x-1)^2 = k`.
Let `g(x) = x(x-1)^2`.
For `x \in [0, 1/3]`, `g(x)` is increasing.
`g(0) = 0`.
`g(1/3) = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27`.
Since `k \in [0, 4/27]`, there exists a unique root in `[0, 1/3]`.
Since `a \le b \le c`, `a` must be the smallest root.
Since `g(x)` is increasing on `[0, 1/3]` and `g(a) = k`, and `0 \le k \le 4/27`, we have `g(0) \le g(a) \le g(1/3)`, which implies `0 \le a \le 1/3`.

To formalize this:
`a` is a root of `x(x-1)^2 = k`.
If `a < 0`, then `a(a-1)^2 < 0`, but `k \ge 0`.
If `a > 1/3`, then since `a \le b \le c`, all roots are `> 1/3`.
If all roots are `> 1/3`, then their sum `a+b+c > 1`, which is not a contradiction yet.
However, `g(x)` has local max at `1/3` with value `4/27` and local min at `1` with value `0`.
The equation `g(x) = k` for `k \in [0, 4/27]` has three roots: one in `[0, 1/3]`, one in `[1/3, 1]`, and one in `[1, 4/3]`.
Since `a \le b \le c`, we must have `a \in [0, 1/3]`.

The objective is to prove `0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1 / 3` given the context.
We are given:
- $a \le b \le c$
- $a + b + c = 2$
- $ab + bc + ca = 1$
- The polynomial $f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c) = x(x-1)^2 - k$, where $k = abc$.
- Roots $a, b, c$ are the intersection points of $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ and the horizontal line $y = k$.
- $0 \le k \le 4/27$ (from `h_k_range`).

Let's analyze $g(x) = x(x-1)^2 = x^3 - 2x^2 + x$.
$g'(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 1 = (3x-1)(x-1)$.
Critical points are $x = 1/3$ and $x = 1$.
$g(0) = 0$.
$g(1/3) = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
$g(1) = 0$.

Since $k \in [0, 4/27]$, the horizontal line $y=k$ intersects $g(x)$ at three points (the roots $a, b, c$).
Looking at the graph of $g(x)$:
- For $x \in [0, 1/3]$, $g(x)$ increases from $0$ to $4/27$. Thus the smallest root $a$ must satisfy $g(a) = k \in [0, 4/27]$, so $a \in [0, 1/3]$.
- For $x \in [1/3, 1]$, $g(x)$ decreases from $4/27$ to $0$. Thus $b \in [1/3, 1]$.
- For $x \ge 1$, $g(x)$ increases from $0$ to $\infty$. Thus $c \ge 1$.

The subgoal is specifically `0 ≤ a ∧ a ≤ 1/3`.
Given $g(a) = k$ and $k \ge 0$, since $a \le b \le c$, $a$ is the smallest root.
Since $g(x)$ is strictly increasing on $[0, 1/3]$ from $0$ to $4/27$, and $k \in [0, 4/27]$, there is exactly one root in $[0, 1/3]$.
Also $g(1/3) = 4/27 \ge k = g(a)$. Since $g$ is increasing on $[0, 1/3]$, if $a$ were $> 1/3$, the other roots would have to be elsewhere, but $a$ is the smallest root.

Wait, $a, b, c$ are roots of $x(x-1)^2 = k$.
$a \le b \le c$.
If $0 \le k \le 4/27$:
$g(0) = 0 \le k$
$g(1/3) = 4/27 \ge k$
$g(1) = 0 \le k$
$g(4/3) = (4/3)(1/3)^2 = 4/27 \ge k$.
The roots are in $[0, 1/3]$, $[1/3, 1]$, and $[1, 4/3]$.
Since $a$ is the smallest, $a \in [0, 1/3]$.

To prove $a \ge 0$:
$a(a-1)^2 = k$. Since $k \ge 0$ (from `h_k_range`) and $(a-1)^2 \ge 0$, then $a \ge 0$ (unless $a-1=0$, but then $k=0$ and $a=1$, but $a$ is the smallest root and $a+b+c=2$, so $a=1 \implies b,c \ge 1 \implies a+b+c \ge 3$, contradiction).
To prove $a \le 1/3$:
$g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ is increasing on $[0, 1/3]$. $g(a) = k \le 4/27 = g(1/3)$.
If $a > 1/3$, then $b$ and $c$ would also be $> 1/3$.
Actually, since $a \le b \le c$, if $a > 1/3$, then $g(x) = k$ would have no roots $\le 1/3$. But for $k \le 4/27$, there is always a root in $[0, 1/3]$.
Thus $a \le 1/3$.

I will use the property that $a$ is a root of $x^3 - 2x^2 + x - k = 0$.
Specifically, $(a-1)^2 a = k \ge 0 \implies a \ge 0$.
And $g(a) = k \le 4/27$. Since $a \le b \le c$ and $g$ peaks at $1/3$, $a$ must be in the first interval.
More formally, $f(x) = (x-a)(x-b)(x-c)$.
$f(0) = -abc = -k \le 0$.
$f(1/3) = (1/3)(1/3-1)^2 - k = 4/27 - k \ge 0$.
By IVT, there is a root in $[0, 1/3]$. Since $a$ is the smallest root, $a \le 1/3$ and $0 \le a$.
Wait, $f(0) \le 0$ and $f(1/3) \ge 0$ implies there is a root $r \in [0, 1/3]$.
Since $a$ is the minimum root, $a \le r \le 1/3$.
Also $f(x) < 0$ for $x < a$. Since $f(0) = -k \le 0$, if $k > 0$, then $0 \ge a$. If $k=0$, then $a=0$.
Wait, if $k \ge 0$, then $f(0) = -k \le 0$. Since $\lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x) = -\infty$, the smallest root $a$ must satisfy $f(x) \le 0$ for $x \le a$.
Actually, for a cubic with $a \le b \le c$, $f(x) \le 0$ for $x \in (-\infty, a]$.
So $f(0) = -k \le 0$ implies $0$ is in $(-\infty, a] \cup [b, c]$.
But $k \le 4/27$ means $f(1/3) = 4/27 - k \ge 0$.
In a cubic, $f(x) \ge 0$ for $x \in [a, b] \cup [c, \infty)$.
So $1/3 \in [a, b] \cup [c, \infty)$.
Since $a \le 1/3$ (because $f(0) \le 0$ and $f(1/3) \ge 0$ and $f$ is continuous), $a \le 1/3$.
And $f(0) = -k \le 0$ and $f(a) = 0$ with $f$ increasing on $(-\infty, 1/3]$ implies $a \ge 0$.
Actually $g(x) = x(1-x)^2$. $g(a) = k$.
If $a < 0$, then $g(a) < 0$, but $k \ge 0$. So $a \ge 0$.
If $a > 1/3$, then since $a \le b \le c$, all roots are $> 1/3$.
Then $f(1/3) = (1/3-a)(1/3-b)(1/3-c) < 0$ (product of 3 negatives).
But $f(1/3) = 4/27 - k \ge 0$. Contradiction. So $a \le 1/3$.

From the cubic $f(x)$, we have $f'(x) = (x-1)^2 + 2x(x-1) = (x-1)(x-1+2x) = (x-1)(3x-1)$.
The critical points are $x = 1/3$ and $x = 1$.
The local maximum of $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ is at $x=1/3$ with $g(1/3) = (1/3)(-2/3)^2 = 4/27$.
The local minimum is at $x=1$ with $g(1) = 0$.
The equation $g(x) = k$ has three real roots $a, b, c$ if and only if $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
By the properties of the graph of $g(x)$:
- The first root $a$ is in $[0, 1/3]$.
- The second root $b$ is in $[1/3, 1]$.
- The third root $c$ is in $[1, 4/3]$ (since $g(4/3) = (4/3)(1/3)^2 = 4/27$).

To prove $1/3 \le b \le 1$, we note that $b$ is the middle root.
$g(x) - k = 0$.
$g(1/3) - k = 4/27 - k \ge 0$ (from $h\_k\_range$).
$g(1) - k = 0 - k = -k \le 0$ (from $h\_k\_range$).
Since $g(x)-k$ is continuous, and $g(1/3)-k \ge 0$ and $g(1)-k \le 0$, there exists a root in $[1/3, 1]$.
Since $a \le 1/3$ and $c \ge 1$, the root in $[1/3, 1]$ must be $b$.

        by_contra h_lt
        push_neg at h_lt
        -- If b < 1/3, then since a <= b, a < 1/3.
        -- f is increasing on [0, 1/3]. So f(a) <= f(b) < f(1/3) = 4/27.
        -- But f(a) = f(b) = f(c) = k.
        -- This contradicts that c is the largest root?
        -- Actually, a, b are the two smaller roots. In [0, 1], f(x) = k has at most 2 roots.
        -- For f(x)=k to have two roots in [0, 1], k must be <= 4/27.
        -- The roots are separated by the local max at 1/3. One in [0, 1/3], one in [1/3, 1].
        -- Since a <= b and both are in [0, 1] (as f(x) < 0 for x < 0), 
        -- we must have a <= 1/3 and b >= 1/3.
        have f_deriv : deriv f = λ x => 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 := by
          ext x
          unfold f
          rw [deriv_mul (by Intros; exact differentiableAt_id') (by Intros; exact DifferentiableAt.pow (DifferentiableAt.sub (differentiableAt_id') (differentiableAt_const 1)) 2)]
          simp; ring
        have f_mono : StrictMonoOn f (Set.Icc 0 (1/3)) := by
          apply strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos (convex_Icc 0 (1/3))
          · apply Continuous.continuousOn; continuity
          · intros x hx; simp at hx
            rw [f_deriv]
            let x_val := x
            have : 3 * x^2 - 4 * x + 1 = (3 * x - 1) * (x - 1) := by ring
            rw [this]
            apply mul_pos_of_neg_of_neg
            · linarith [hx.2]
            · linarith [hx.2]
        if ha0 : 0 ≤ a then
          have h_fab : f a = f b := by rw [hb]; have := h_poly a; simp at this; rw [this]; ring
          by_contra h_blt
          push_neg at h_blt
          have hb_pos : 0 ≤ b := by
            by_contra hb_neg; push_neg at hb_neg
            have : f b < 0 := by unfold f; nlinarith
            linarith [h_k_range.1, hb]
          have : a = b := f_mono.eq_iff_eq (Set.Icc_subset_Icc (le_refl 0) (by linarith) ⟨ha0, by linarith⟩) ⟨hb_pos, by linarith⟩ |>.mp h_fab
          -- This doesn't directly give a contradiction, but f(x)=k on [0, 1] 
          -- has at most one root in [0, 1/3) and one in (1/3, 1].
          -- If b < 1/3, then a and b are both in [0, 1/3], so a=b.
          -- Then f(x) - k = (x-a)^2 (x-c). 
          -- Expansion gives 2a + c = 2, a^2 + 2ac = 1.
          -- Sub c = 2-2a: a^2 + 2a(2-2a) = 1 => 3a^2 - 4a + 1 = 0 => (3a-1)(a-1) = 0.
          -- a = 1/3 (so b=1/3) or a = 1 (not possible as a <= 1/3).
          -- Thus b must be >= 1/3.
          let k := a * b * c
          have h_eq : 3*b^2 - 4*b + 1 ≤ 0 := by
            -- Since f(b) = k and k is the max value 4/27 or less,
            -- and b is the middle root, b must be between the local max and min.
            -- Local max of x(x-1)^2 is at 1/3, min at 1.
            -- For 3 roots to exist, k in [0, 4/27].
            -- Roots are in [0, 1/3], [1/3, 1], [1, 4/3].
            admit
          linarith [h_eq]
        else admit
      · -- Show b <= 1
        by_contra h_gt
        push_neg at h_gt
        have : f b > 0 := by admit -- Since f(1)=0 and f increases for x > 1
        have : f b = a * b * c := hb
        -- For x > 1, f(x) is strictly increasing.
        -- Since c >= b > 1, if b > 1, then f(c) >= f(b) > 0.
        -- However, f(x) = k has 3 roots. $g(x)=k$ has 2 roots in [0,1] and 1 in [1, 4/3].
        -- If b > 1, then b and c are both in [1, 4/3].
        -- But g(x) is strictly increasing on [1, \infty).
        -- So b = c. Similar to above, this forces b = 1.
        admit
  
    have h_c_bounds : 1 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 4 / 3 := by
      admit
  
    exact ⟨h_a_bounds.1, h_a_bounds.2, h_b_bounds.1, h_b_bounds.2, h_c_bounds.1, h_c_bounds.2⟩
```<think>
The goal is to prove $1/3 \le b \le 1$ given $a, b, c$ are roots of $f(x) = x(x-1)^2 - k = 0$ with $k = abc$, $a \le b \le c$, and $0 \le k \le 4/27$.
The function $g(x) = x(x-1)^2$ has a local maximum at $x=1/3$ where $g(1/3) = (1/3)(2/3)^2 = 4/27$ and a local minimum at $x=1$ where $g(1) = 0$.
The roots of $g(x) - k = 0$ are $a, b, c$.
Since $0 \le k \le 4/27$:
1. $a$ is in the interval $[0, 1/3]$ because $g$ is increasing on $[0, 1/3]$ from $0$ to $4/27$.
2. $b$ is in the interval $[1/3, 1]$ because $g$ is decreasing on $[1/3, 1]$ from $4/27$ to $0$.
3. $c$ is in the interval $[1, 4/3]$ (approximately, actually up to $1 + 1/\sqrt{3}$ but constrained by $a+b+c=2$).
Specifically for $b$, since $g(b) = k$ and $b \in [a, c]$, and $g$ decreases from $1/3$ to $1$, the middle root $b$ must lie in $[1/3, 1]$.
I will use the properties of the cubic $x(x-1)^2 - k$.
